paragraphs: Mentioned in [Arakhin 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.11a.17), transmitting a teaching in Rabbi Yochanan’s name; [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Arakhin.11a.17.1) explains that this is a sage's name. There, [28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.28b.8), Chizkiyah bar Biluto may be his son. Perhaps his own name was Shimon, as at [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim, the beginning of chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.4.1.5): Rabbi Shimon Bulota in Rabbi Chanina's name.[^1]

notes.text: The linked sources use different forms of the name. In Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim, Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha and Rabbi Shimon Bulota are named in a transmission in Rabbi Chanina’s name. The suggested father–son relationship and identification with Shimon are Hyman’s conjectures.
